title: Tiered latency bench harness and prefill-priority evaluator
creator: Amir Patel
description: Build a next-gen benchmarking harness that evaluates kernel selection and attention-path optimizations across multiple latency SLO tiers, and validates a prefill-priority scheduling policy. Deliverables: (1) a suite of synthetic + replayed workloads partitioned into latency tiers (interactive / bursted / throughput), (2) automated golden baseline capture and artifact storage for each tier and model variant, (3) CI perf gates with deterministic regression detection and automated alerting, and (4) an evaluator that scores prefill vs decode scheduling trade-offs using cost and tail-latency metrics.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Harness can run 3 canonical workloads (interactive-low-latency, bursty-prefill-heavy, high-throughput-batch) against a model matrix and produce artifact bundles (metrics, traces, kernel-selection logs).
A2: Golden baselines are recorded to s3://redwood-bench/gold/runtime-1.24/{tier}/{model}/{commit} and include p50/p90/p99 latencies, tokens/s, kernel-selection histograms, and KV cache hit rates.

A3: CI perf gate integration: PRs that change runtime/kernel-routing fail if p99 latency regression > 5ms for interactive tier or throughput drop >3% for throughput tier, with noise filtering via 5-run median and bootstrap CI.

A4: Prefill-priority evaluator outputs a ranked policy table (score = weighted function of expected tail-latency savings and token-cost delta) and a sample set of recommended policy parameters per model family.
A5: Documentation and runbook added to Confluence with how to add new workloads, interpret artifacts, and triage CI gate failures.
technical_notes: Workloads: combine synthetic prompt templates (lengths 8-2048) + production trace replay (sampled 0.5%) with request distribution shaping per tier.
Kernel telemetry: extend kr-profiler to emit per-call kernel_id, sequence_length, attention-pattern-tag, and execution-time-ms; attach to bench artifacts.

Prefill scheduling: implement a simulated prefill-priority scheduler in harness that can toggle priorities, preemption windows, and KV-cache warming heuristics to measure tail impact without changing live scheduler.
Golden baseline capture: produce deterministic seeds, fixed cluster config, and run 5 warmup iterations then 20 measurement iterations; store raw traces + aggregated summaries.
CI gating: use bot-run isolated CI runners with pinned hardware profile (A100-80GB equiv) and compare against latest approved golden baseline using permutation test + bootstrap for p-values.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Kickoff with performance and infra -> agreed on three target latency tiers and canonical models (gpt-open-7b, rwx-13b, rwx-70b).
2026-03-02: Prototype runner that replays production traces in a containerized harness; initial kernel telemetry added to kr-profiler (PR #4921).

2026-03-05: First synthetic workload runs show kernel-selection variance across sequence lengths; observed 12% throughput regression when forcing legacy kernel for short sequences — captured artifacts.
2026-03-08: Design review with PM (Sofia Martinez) and Observability -> agreed golden artifact schema and s3 path layout; identified need for noise-reduction protocol in CI.
2026-03-11: Created draft CI job (runtime/bench-gate) that runs harness on PR merge; smoke pass completes but needs bootstrap stats and auto-bisect disabled until noise reduced.
decisions: D1: Use three explicit tiers (interactive: p99 SLO tight, burst: prefill-heavy, throughput: aggregate tokens/sec focused) instead of a continuous distribution to simplify gates and on-call triage.
D2: Store golden baselines per model+quantization+kernel-profile to avoid masking regressions caused by kernel routing changes.
D3: CI gate will fail only on sustained regressions (median of N runs with bootstrap CI) to reduce flakiness and pager noise.
risks: R1: CI noise due to shared hardware variance could produce false positives — mitigated by dedicated runners and bootstrap-based thresholds.
R2: Large S3 artifact storage growth; mitigate with retention policy and delta-encoding for golden baselines.
R3: Simulator prefill policy might not capture all behaviors of real scheduler; will validate with small canary on Dedicated cluster before rollout.
notes: Goal is to make kernel-routing and prefill scheduling changes observable via repeatable bench artifacts and to reduce regressions making it to production by adding defensible CI gates. Next: stabilize CI noise and finalize golden baseline retention policy.
